notes: לְמֹשֶׁה is rendered by the bare genitive Moses, so the preposition fuses with the name under rule 49's last clause; the copula stays with הָיָה, which is written.

The it of it was is a referential subject pronoun realizing the verb's own person and number (rule 17) rather than rule 21's dummy; the unit is identical either way, so the alignment stands as accepted.
The לְ of לְמָנָה has no English word in the recasting and is unrepresented (rules 21, 40).
